maml:description.maml:para: Appends one or more data rows to an existing Excel table.

Use this command when a workbook already contains a named table and the script should extend that table without recreating the worksheet through the Excel DSL. The command accepts a workbook path, an open ExcelDocument, or an existing ExcelTable object. Objects, dictionaries, DataTable, DataView, IDataReader, and DataRow input are normalized through the same table input pipeline used by Add-OfficeExcelTable.

When a path is supplied, PSWriteOffice opens the workbook, appends the rows, saves the workbook, and releases the document. When an open workbook or table is supplied, the caller controls the lifetime and should close or save the workbook after all edits are complete.
Rows to append. Accepts objects, dictionaries, DataTables, DataViews, IDataReaders, and DataRows.

maml:description.maml:para: Exports a recognized image as editable Excel, Word, text, Markdown, HTML, JSON, CSV or searchable PDF.

Recognize once with Get-OfficeImageDocument, inspect its evidence, then reuse that snapshot for each output. Excel and CSV contain detected tables only. CSV requires exactly one table. Empty recognition or missing tables fail before output publication.

CSV field formatting and formula policy. When omitted, formula-like source text is escaped, including negative numeric text. Supplied options retain their FormulaInjectionPolicy; a new CsvSaveOptions object defaults to Preserve. Set Escape explicitly when customizing options for spreadsheet consumption.

Every recognized table row is written as data without a synthesized header, regardless of IncludeHeader. This command controls UTF-8, uncompressed file output and replacement through Force; CsvOptions controls field formatting and formula handling.

dev:remarks.maml:para: Formats ID values as text, Revenue as currency, Rate as a one-decimal percentage, and Created as a short date while keeping formatting logic in OfficeIMO.

maml:description.maml:para: Adds native password encryption or editing restrictions to a document.

Supports PDF and Open XML Word, Excel and PowerPoint packages. Path input is saved in place unless OutputPath names a protected copy. File inputs must be unencrypted: this command has no CurrentPassword parameter. Live Word/Excel restrictions may remain in memory; encryption requires OutputPath or a native associated file path. Encryption is a one-time export, not a stored password setting on the live input. PDF protection returns a new native document with preservation proof, leaving the original live PDF intact. Without Encrypt, PDF restrictions use Password or RestrictionPassword as the owner password and allow opening without a password. With Encrypt, a separate owner password keeps the open password from authorizing permission changes. Unsupported restrictions produce warnings; an entirely unsupported request writes nothing. Safe native signature and preservation policies remain in force.
Encrypt the saved artifact using its native engine.

Excel tables accept LegacyPasswordHash, ModifyPasswordHash and ReservedBy; native workbook and reservation property tables are also accepted. PDF tables accept Algorithm, EncryptMetadata, Permissions or AllowedPermissions, and AesCryptographyProvider. Supply PDF passwords through Password and RestrictionPassword. Typed native PDF options retain their owner password, permission mask, algorithm, metadata setting and AES provider.
Protected file destination; accepts exactly one input when supplied.
